text:
maya: Heads up — saw two KV OOMs on prod gpool-7 at ~09:12. Both coincide with large continuous batches after the new kernel-selector rollout (v2). Putting logs and quick profile here so we can decide admission behavior.

josh: Can you paste the log snippet? which requests triggered it?

maya: sure — here's the tail from the worker that OOMed:```
[09:12:31] batch_assembler: forming batch id=0x7fb size=1024 tokens total_kv=1.9GB
[09:12:31] kv_cache: mem_usage=3.7GB limit=4.0GB (frag=0.12)
[09:12:32] kernel-selector: chose v2-fused-attn for seq=2048
[09:12:32] batch_executor: kv_alloc failed, oom when reserving 128MB for kv-window
[09:12:32] oom_guard: triggered soft-shed, but too late
```

maya: The pattern: kernel-selector chooses faster fused kernels that result in slightly larger KV working set during the assembly window. Batches were greedy and hit the soft limit.

arya: Thanks. This smells like we need admission-time KV-awareness: don't just cap by token-count but also estimate kv_delta per request (using model & seq len). We already have a heuristic per-model kv_factor in experiments.

josh: Agreed. Current admission uses: `target_tokens_per_batch` and `max_batch_size` only. No per-request kv estimate. Adding `kv_estimate = kv_factor * seq_len` to the admission scoring would help.

tom: Proposal: implement a two-tier admission: 1) a fast path uses tokens-only when kv_free > high_water; 2) a conservative kv-aware cap when kv_free between high_water and soft_limit. Pseudocode:```
if (kv_free > high_water) admit_by_tokens();
else { // kv pressure
  for req in queue: if (kv_estimate(req) + batch_kv <= kv_budget) admit else defer
}```

li: Also consider preemptive soft-eviction of cold KV entries when kv_free < reclaim_threshold *and* batch window estimated to exceed X ms. We should avoid evicting hot entries during active decoding though.

maya: Important: we need admission that doesn't block small latency-critical requests. So prefer admitting small short-seq requests even under kv pressure. Maybe a tiny priority boost for request_age < 50ms and seq_len < 128.

josh: Quick experiment idea: run a synthetic mix with current kernel v2 + baseline admission vs. kv-aware admission and measure: 95p latency, tail OOMs, and throughput. We should also test with kernel v1 (smaller kv footprint) to separate kernel vs. admission effects.

infra-bot: CI perf job ran for branch `frugal-batcher`. Summary: throughput -2.3% (within noise), p95 +1.8% on small seqs, p99 unchanged. No OOMs in 30m soak with kv-aware admission enabled. Full logs: https://ci.internal/runs/9753

arya: Good sign that kv-aware admission prevents OOMs. But p95 regression on small seqs is worrying. Maybe our conservative cap is too aggressive. We should tune `kv_budget_fraction` used for batch admission.

tom: Another knob: allow transient overcommit for at-most-one-batch-per-worker as long as we have a fallback to preempt it (soft-fallback) if actual kv allocation grows. So optimistic admission + fast preemption. But preemption complexity is higher.

li: On preemption: we can implement a cheap 'reclaim token' where decoding checkpoints and frees intermediate KV for speculative work — heavy engineering. For now prefer throttling.

maya: Action items: 1) Josh to add kv_estimate into admission scoring and a `kv_budget_fraction` flag (default 0.85) — run soak. 2) Tom to prototype conservative queue policy (high_water / soft_limit thresholds). 3) Arya & Li to draft soft-eviction fallback plan. 4) I'll run A/B with kernel v1 vs v2 to separate signals.

josh: I'll open PR with the kv_estimate patch and a microbenchmark harness. Expect initial numbers by EOD.

maya: Thanks. If anyone sees repeated OOMs, please escalate to incidents and pin worker with dump. Also tagging @tom for follow-up on queue policy tuning. :thinking_face: 

tom: noted, will follow up with a short RFC once we have PR numbers.

infra-bot: alert: job `soak-frugal-batcher-2` reached 6h without OOM after patch deployment to staging.
